reasoning_trace: Read the witness monitor output first, blind: no event at all. Since this fault type didn't produce an infra-level signal, searched more broadly for AML-domain keywords instead of assuming another crash-shaped pattern. Found a direct, unambiguous, self-reported event: aml-compliance logged AML_SANCTIONS_HIT for payment 450eefbc (matchedEntity='TREN DE ARAGUA', matchScore=1.0, durationMs=7) immediately followed by AML_HOLD amlState=ESCALATED for the same payment, both timestamped 0.17s after the injection time. A second, separate real match fired later in the same window (payment f085c800, matchedEntity='Arian Bank Afghanistan', matchScore=0.93, amlState=HOLD). This is qualitatively different evidence from every crash-fault case investigated so far: the service directly announces its own decisive action in its own log stream, rather than requiring an external witness or a funnel-stall inference. No other service shows any anomaly in the window. Conclusion reached from evidence alone, before reading the injector's own log: aml-compliance.
confirmation_basis: Blind conclusion (aml-compliance) matches the injector's own ground-truth log exactly. Directly self-reported by the service in its own real log stream (AML_SANCTIONS_HIT + AML_HOLD events), the strongest and most direct evidence class seen in this dataset so far -- no external witness or inference needed, unlike every crash-fault case.
